newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen heading up, breaking more records.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen heading up, breaking more records.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to break more records on Tuesday with funds flowing into the market and derivatives traders eager to buy up the futures market ahead of Thursday's settlement, brokers said.

"The chance of a steep market surge today probably is not big after Monday's major gains but it's difficult to tell since it's a liquidity-driven market," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed 242.96 points, or 1.70 percent, higher at a record 14,574.64 on Monday on record turnover of HK$20.59 billion.
Brokers said intra-day profit-taking should trim gains as there were no trading clues form New York or London markets, which were closed on Monday for holidays.

"Focus should still be on red chips since Chinese and overseas money has shifted from the Chinese B-share markets to China-backed companies listed in Hong Kong," said Antony Mak, a sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The blue-chip index was expected to fluctuate at high levels until there were signs of a retreat of hot money, brokers said.
